title: Get started
description: Requirements, installation, and the first steps for a Troolio host.
text:
Get started 
 Troolio 10.0.6 is a .NET 10 framework for event-sourced actors on Microsoft Orleans 10. This path gets you from a package reference to a small actor, then points to the host and provider decisions that make a real application work. 
 Before you begin 
 
 Install the .NET 10 SDK. Use a .NET 10 runtime for the host. 
 Keep Microsoft Orleans packages on the 10.x line across the application. 
 Review and accept the license included in each Troolio package. 
 Decide whether this is a local learning host or a serving application. In-memory storage is useful for local examples and loses data on process exit. 
 
 Install the foundation 
 Create a project, then add the framework and Orleans build tooling. The exact version avoids mixing the five-package cohort with older builds. 
 dotnet new classlib -n MyApp -f net10.0
cd MyApp
dotnet add package Troolio.Core --version 10.0.6
dotnet add package Microsoft.Orleans.Sdk --version 10.0.0
 
 Add a provider only when the host needs it: 
 dotnet add package Troolio.SqlServer --version 10.0.6
# or
dotnet add package Troolio.KurrentDB --version 10.0.6
 
 Use the  package guide  for the roles and dependencies of all five packages. A SQL Server or KurrentDB reference does not install a production schema or select a serving route. 
 Follow the first application path 
 
 Build your first actor  with a command, an event, an event handler, and a query. The example compiles against the packaged 10.0.6 binaries. 
 Configure a host  with actor assembly registration, a store, a serializer, and Orleans services. 
 Read  actors and commands  and  events and state  before choosing a persistence provider. 
 For an explicitly selected atomic path, review  the selected command route  and  atomic commit  together. The route needs compatible store capabilities, authority, projection handoffs, and recovery. 
 Plan for  security and retention  and  deployment  before serving real callers. 
 
 What the package does and what the host does 
 Troolio supplies actor and event contracts, command dispatch, storage abstractions, and opt-in provider surfaces. The application host authenticates callers, authorizes the current command and target, configures credentials, selects a route, operates projection and recovery workers, and sets evidence and idempotency retention windows. Installing a package by itself activates none of those decisions. 
 
 Source note for maintainers:   Build.props ,  Troolio.Core/package-readme.md , the five project files, and  probes/ProductionPackageConsumer/README.md  define this compatibility and package boundary.

title: Actors and commands
description: Actor roles, typed commands, queries, and dispatch.
text:
Actors and commands 
 Troolio uses Microsoft Orleans actors as the command boundary. An actor interface extends  IActor ; a concrete actor handles typed messages and keeps the current state derived from its event history.  CqrsActor ,  EventSourcedActor ,  StatefulActor ,  ProjectionActor , and  OrchestrationActor  serve different roles rather than interchangeable base classes. 
 Command path 
 A  Command<TActor>  addresses a specific actor contract. A handler named  Handle  returns zero or more domain events. The actor dispatches those events to  On  handlers to update its in-memory state. Queries use  Query<TActor,TResult>  and a typed handler to read that current state.  The first actor guide  has a compiled example. 
 InternalCommand<TActor>  is used for framework and orchestration work inside the actor system. A serving host still has to decide which external commands it permits, authenticate the caller, and authorize the target. Message  Metadata  carries correlation and identity fields; it is trace context, not proof of current authorization. 
 Actor roles 
 
 
 
 Role 
 Typical responsibility 
 
 
 
 
 Event sourced actor 
 Replays a stream, handles commands, emits events, and answers queries. 
 
 
 Stateful actor 
 Maintains state from subscribed events for internal orchestration. 
 
 
 Projection actor 
 Consumes events to update a read model outside the command transaction. 
 
 
 Orchestration actor 
 Reacts to events and may issue internal commands. 
 
 
 Dispatch actor 
 Provides typed message dispatch without selecting a persistence policy. 
 
 
 
 Ordinary and selected command paths 
 The ordinary actor path appends to its configured store and dispatches events according to host configuration. A separately selected atomic path plans a closed participant set and requires a capable transaction store, route authority, and completion receipt. Do not infer selected-route guarantees from an ordinary  Command  call. Read  selected command route  before using it. 
 Design checks 
 
 Keep command handlers focused on deciding events. Historical event replay must be free of external side effects. 
 Treat an empty event result as a meaningful no-change outcome only when the selected route's completion store supports it. 
 Use stable actor IDs and version expectations. A store rejects stale expected versions rather than silently overwriting history. 
 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Messages.cs ,  CqrsActor.cs ,  EventSourcedActor.cs ,  DispatchActor.cs ,  Stateful/ ,  ProjectionActor.cs , and  OrchestrationActor.cs .

title: Events and state
description: Event history, state replay, and lifecycle.
text:
Events, state, and snapshots 
 Events are the durable record of domain changes. An event sourced actor replays its stream when activated and applies events to rebuild current in-memory state. State fields and read models are derived views; they do not replace the event stream as the write history. 
 Event identity 
 Event  inherits  Message , so it carries  Metadata : correlation ID, user ID, device ID, message ID, and optional transaction and causation IDs. An  EventEnvelope<T>  adds event ID, stream, and version for downstream delivery. Those values support tracing and ordering; the serving host must still establish current caller and source authority before dispatch. 
 Replay 
 On activation,  EventSourcedActor  initializes and replays stored events. Event  On  handlers must produce the same state from the same history and should not send provider requests, notifications, or commands as a replay side effect. Store append and actor state are separate concerns: if a commit outcome is uncertain, deactivate and reconcile against the durable head before treating memory as current. 
 Stateful views and snapshots 
 EventSourcedActor<TState>  and the stateful actor types provide a typed state shape. The  State/ ,  Stateful/ , and  Snapshots/  source areas define state and snapshot messages. Snapshot policy and storage belong to the host and provider configuration. A snapshot speeds replay only if it is verifiably tied to the preceding event history; it is not an independent source of truth. 
 Actor creation is a separate lifecycle concern.  CreatableActor  and creation command contracts distinguish an absent actor from an existing stream. Plan explicit first-write and retry behavior; do not assume that every command can create an actor. 
 Versioning and schema evolution 
 IStore.Append  accepts an expected event version. A mismatch must reject the append. When event types or serialization formats evolve, keep historical payloads readable and validate a replay of old streams before deploying writers that produce the new format. The framework supplies serializer implementations, while your application owns event schema compatibility. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Messages.cs ,  EventSourcedActor.cs ,  EventSourcedActor.State.cs ,  Stateful/ ,  State/ ,  Snapshots/ ,  Creatable/ , and  Stores/IStore.cs .

title: Stores and serialization
description: Persistence contracts and event formats.
text:
Stores and serialization 
 IStore  is the base event-stream contract. It appends a collection of events at an expected stream version and reads all, a range, the last event, or one event. A store implementation determines durability, concurrency behavior, and its deployment requirements. 
 Store choices 
 
 
 
 Store 
 Intended use 
 
 
 
 
 InMemoryStore 
 Local examples and tests; state disappears with the process. 
 
 
 FileSystemStore 
 Local filesystem experiments; review filesystem semantics before relying on it. 
 
 
 Troolio.SqlServer 
 SQL Server adapters with explicit schema, transaction, and recovery setup. 
 
 
 Troolio.KurrentDB 
 KurrentDB append and named-stream integration with separate route and recovery contracts. 
 
 
 
 The two bundled Core stores do not grant the selected atomic transaction capability. That route requires  IAtomicEventTransactionStore  and, when fenced,  IRouteFencedAtomicEventTransactionStore  with the required capability flags.  Atomic commit  explains the full contract. 
 Serializer options 
 Core includes  JsonEventSerializer ,  MessagePackEventSerializer , and  MessagePackLz4EventSerializer  behind  IEventSerializer . Choose one deliberately, test round trips of your domain event types, and retain backward readers for any stored format you have already written. Changing serializers without migration can make historical replay fail. 
 Orleans serialization attributes on message records serve actor transport. They do not by themselves define the bytes your chosen event store writes. The store's serializer and the application event schema must agree. 
 Operational contract 
 The store must enforce expected versions and return an append count consistent with what it committed. For the selected route, the store must atomically commit participant events, required projection handoffs, ancillary writes, and completion evidence. A  IStore  implementation alone does not promise that stronger property. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Stores/IStore.cs ,  InMemoryStore.cs ,  FileSystemStore.cs ,  Stores/Serialization/ , and  Stores/IAtomicEventTransactionStore.cs .

title: Streams and subscriptions
description: Event streams, subscriptions, and queues.
text:
Streams and subscriptions 
 Troolio uses Orleans streams and broadcast channels to move event envelopes toward projection and orchestration consumers. Subscription attributes connect a consumer to events from an actor type or name; they are routing declarations, not a durable completion receipt. 
 Projection subscriptions 
 ProjectionStreamSubscriptionAttribute  matches a projection stream namespace derived from an actor type or actor name. Projection actors resume stream subscriptions and process  IEventEnvelope  messages. The source actor's append can complete before the read model reflects that event; design callers for eventual consistency. 
 Orchestration subscriptions 
 OrchestrationStreamSubscriptionAttribute  serves orchestration listeners. An orchestration handler may issue internal commands that produce more events. A broadcast publish alone does not prove that every expected handler has finished, that nested work is registered, or that an event-only transaction is closed. 
 When atomic closure is required 
 Selected event-only routes require a reviewed subscriber manifest and a durable closure protocol. The manifest must account for the deployed binding inventory and handler effect classification. Completion receipts are recorded only after expected handlers and child work finish. Read  orchestration  and  selected command route  before using those surfaces. 
 Host responsibilities 
 Configure stream providers and subscription lifecycle in the host. Monitor consumer lag and recover pending durable handoffs. Keep a stable deployment/binding version during a selected route, and reject drift before commit. Do not use stream delivery as a substitute for store transaction guarantees. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Streams/ ,  ProjectionStreamSubscriptions.cs ,  ProjectionActor.cs ,  OrchestrationActor.cs , and  Transactions/OrleansBroadcastRegistrationInventory.cs .

title: Projections and read models
description: Asynchronous views over committed events.
text:
Projections and read models 
 Projections turn committed events into query-focused views. They run after the command's durable write boundary, so a successful command does not imply an immediately updated read model. 
 The handoff boundary 
 A selected atomic store commits required projection handoffs with participant events and completion evidence. Projection workers later consume those handoffs, apply read-model changes, and record progress. If a worker fails, the handoff remains available for recovery. The host chooses and operates the consumers; Troolio does not start a production read-side service merely because a package is installed. 
 The ordinary route can use inline or configured outbox dispatch. When  ProjectionDispatch:Mode  selects  OutboxPrimary  for an actor, the store must report that it atomically commits dispatch with events. The actor rejects that configuration if the store cannot meet the contract. 
 Read model actors 
 ProjectionActor  and  ReadModelProjectionActor<T>  consume event envelopes.  TroolioReadModel  and  ReadModelResolver  are query-side building blocks. Link events can track how a read model relates to a source stream. A read-model schema is application-owned; preserve idempotent processing and version checks when workers retry. 
 What clients should expect 
 Read-side lag is normal. If an API needs read-your-write behavior, the application must design a receipt/version wait or another explicit query strategy. A client notification channel such as Server-Sent Events belongs to the host's projection integration and should not hold an accepted business command open. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/ProjectionActor.cs ,  ReadModels/ ,  ProjectionStreamSubscriptions.cs ,  EventSourcedActor.cs ,  Stores/IStore.cs , and  Troolio.SqlServer/SqlAtomicProjectionConsumer.cs .

title: Reliable jobs
description: Queue-backed jobs and reminder boundaries.
text:
Background jobs and queueing 
 Core includes a  BatchJobActor  and message queue abstractions for queued actor commands. Treat this as a separate background path from the selected atomic command transaction and external effect intent protocol. 
 Queue contract 
 IMessageQueueProvider  supplies a client for a named queue.  BatchJobActor  places a batch job on that queue, uses a timer and reminder to wake processing, and tracks dequeue attempts against the job's retry limit. The configured queue provider determines persistence, visibility, and failure behavior. 
 InMemoryMessageQueueProvider  is process-local and is appropriate for tests or local evaluation. It does not give a durable, multi-silo queue. A serving deployment must choose a provider with the retention and retry semantics it needs and prove the worker lifecycle under process loss. 
 Retry boundaries 
 A retry can repeat a command or provider call after an uncertain outcome. Use stable operation IDs and the selected route's exact completion evidence for business commands. For external effects, the provider must enforce durable idempotency and return terminal receipts for known outcomes. Queue attempt count alone is not an exactly-once guarantee. 
 The older  ReliableActor  source is commented out and should not be treated as an active runtime component. Use  BatchJobActor  only after reviewing its queue provider and error handling for your deployment. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Reliable/BatchJobActor.cs ,  Reliable/Interfaces/ ,  Reliable/Messages/ ,  MessageQueue/ , and  Transactions/ExternalEffectIntent.cs .

title: Selected command route
description: Admission and planning for atomic command execution.
text:
Selected command route 
 A selected command route is an opt-in path for commands whose event writes and related handoffs must close together. It binds one authenticated operation to one root actor, a current deployment route, a complete event plan, and a capable store. Ordinary actor commands remain available; installing an adapter does not select this path. 
 From ingress to completion 
 
 Authenticate the caller and authorize the command, actor, and route at ingress. The host supplies the current principal; message metadata alone is not authority. 
 Create or verify a stable operation ID and canonical request identity.  TrustedAtomicCommandIngressAdapter  and  TrustedAtomicCommandIdentityAuthority  describe this boundary. 
 Acquire the selected route lease and verify the current deployment epoch and fingerprint. Admission can reject a stale silo or an unreviewed actor/handler registration. 
 Plan the root event and any supported causal subscriber events while handlers remain free of external effects. Freeze a closed participant set before storage. 
 Commit with the route fence and expected versions. Return the durable completion receipt only after every required write and projection handoff commits. 
 
 The memory-only path has additional contextual contracts ( MemoryOnlySelectedCommandContext  and  IMemoryOnlyContextualAtomicEventTransactionStore ). “Memory-only” describes precommit planning, not disposable persistence. A failed planner cannot be recovered by replaying a side effect. 
 Route selection checklist 
 Select the route only after reviewing the actor and subscriber inventory, event serialization, store capabilities, recovery policy, provider idempotency, and retention window. Pin the selected deployment and keep the route fence current across promotion or rollback.  Atomic commit ,  route authority , and  recovery  provide the individual contracts. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Transactions/TrustedAtomicCommandIngressAdapter.cs ,  MemoryOnlySelectedCommandContext.cs ,  MemoryOnlyCausalEventCollector.cs , and  SelectedRouteSiloStartupAdmission.cs .

title: Atomic commit
description: Closed event transactions and completion receipts.
text:
Atomic event commit 
 AtomicEventTransaction.CommitAsync  accepts a complete  AtomicEventTransactionRequest . Each participant names an actor path, stream, expected version, and nonempty event list. The request carries one operation ID, a lowercase SHA-256 request identity, and an optional  AtomicRouteFence . 
 Required store behavior 
 The store must implement  IAtomicEventTransactionStore  and advertise  SupportsAtomicEventTransactionsAndProjectionDispatch . It commits  all  participant events, required ancillary streams, projection dispatch handoffs, and the keyed completion receipt as one atomic operation. A selected fenced route also requires  IRouteFencedAtomicEventTransactionStore  and a commit-time comparison of route key, epoch, and deployment fingerprint. 
 Before returning a prior receipt on retry, the store compares the full frozen serialized batch. Reusing an operation ID with changed actor paths, expected versions, event types, or bytes must fail without another append. Current ownership, authorization, and deletion fences still apply to a retry. 
 AtomicEventTransactionReceipt  records committed versions and attests to ancillary writes and projection handoffs. The helper validates that the receipt matches the request and expected final versions. External effects are outside this contract; read  external effects  for the durable intent boundary. 
 No-change outcomes 
 The regular eventful contract rejects an empty participant or empty event list. A durable no-op completion is a separate optional contextual capability with its own receipt shape and root-state checks. Do not manufacture an eventful receipt to represent a no-op. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Stores/IAtomicEventTransactionStore.cs ,  Troolio.Core/Transactions/AtomicEventTransaction.cs ,  MemoryOnlySelectedCommandContext.cs .

title: Route authority
description: Deployment fences, admission, and trust.
text:
Route authority and admission 
 A selected route must know which deployment is allowed to serve it. Troolio represents this with a route key, positive epoch, and deployment fingerprint in  AtomicRouteFence . An authoritative store compares the fence under the same transaction or lock that commits events. Promotion increments the epoch, so an uncommitted request from an older deployment fails. 
 Trust boundaries 
 
 TrustedAtomicCommandIngressAdapter  binds the caller's command to an authenticated route and canonical request identity. 
 IAtomicCommandCurrentPrincipal  supplies current principal evidence; copied message headers do not grant permission. 
 OrleansAtomicNoSubscriberRouteAuthority  and  OrleansAtomicSubscriberRouteAuthority  review actor classes, handlers, and subscriber registrations before a selected path is admitted. 
 IAtomicRouteClusterLeaseAuthority  and selected-route silo admission keep the serving cohort aligned with the deployment record. 
 
 A matching completed receipt can be replayed after promotion only after the current owner/deletion checks and exact request, batch, and route fence comparison. A stale uncommitted request cannot write. The host owns authentication, authorization, process identity, deployment review, and retirement sequencing. 
 Operational use 
 Treat route promotion as a controlled deployment operation. Record the reviewed inventory and fingerprint, admit the new cohort, fence the old epoch, and verify pending operations before retiring it. Provider-specific admission is described in  SQL Server  and  KurrentDB . 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Transactions/TrustedAtomicCommandIngressAdapter.cs ,  TrustedAtomicCommandIdentity.cs ,  OrleansAtomicNoSubscriberRouteAuthority.cs ,  OrleansAtomicSubscriberRouteAuthority.cs , and  IAtomicEventTransactionStore.cs .

title: Orchestration
description: Event-only planning and durable subscriber delivery.
text:
Event-only orchestration 
 An orchestration actor reacts to committed events and coordinates work. Troolio distinguishes ordinary event reactions from a selected event-only closure that plans subscriber results before an atomic event commit. The selected path requires reviewed subscribers, bounded planning, and a store that can persist completion and delivery state. 
 Planning and delivery 
 EventOnlyOrchestrationEnvelope  identifies a source event.  EventOnlyOrchestrationParticipant  captures a planned target stream and expected version. The state store tracks the frozen plan and completion; the delivery store tracks claimable subscriber work.  DurableEventOnlySubscriberExecutor  runs claimed deliveries against registered plan handlers and an emission policy. It validates the plan before committing its events. 
 Handlers in precommit planning must be pure: read approved state and produce deterministic events. Network calls, reminder mutation, and external writes belong behind the  external effect intent  protocol. Bounded depth, event count, and participant count prevent unlimited causal expansion. 
 Failures 
 A claimed delivery may be retried. The operation identity and persisted state keep retries tied to the same source. A definitive handler rejection differs from a transient failure; never silently mark uncertain work complete.  Recovery  explains how to resume pending state. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/OrchestrationActor.cs ,  Transactions/IEventOnlyOrchestrationStateStore.cs ,  IEventOnlyOrchestrationDelivery.cs ,  DurableEventOnlySubscriberExecutor.cs , and  EventOnlyOrchestrationClosure.cs .

title: External effects
description: Durable intents, idempotency, and reminders.
text:
External effects and reminders 
 An atomic event commit does not make a network call, email, or reminder update atomic with event storage. Troolio models such work as an  ExternalEffectIntent  tied to a committed operation, request identity, serialized batch hash, subscriber, provider, and payload hash. 
 Durable intent protocol 
 ExternalEffectDispatcher.RegisterAsync  records a frozen intent after the event receipt is available.  DispatchAsync  calls an  IIdempotentExternalEffectProvider  with a stable key and records a terminal receipt.  RecoverPendingAsync  pages pending intents after restart. A provider must deduplicate by key for the full effect lifetime and return a terminal result only when the outcome is definitive; uncertain failures throw for retry. 
 IAtomicEventEffectIntentStore  supports a stronger path where event commit and effect intent are part of the same transaction, with  AtomicEventEffectTransaction  validating the receipt. A host must choose storage, worker scheduling, provider credentials, retention, and monitoring. If an intent is recorded only after the event commit, the host must account for the gap between those steps. 
 Reminder adapter 
 ReminderEffectIntent  describes register/update or unregister operations.  ReminderDesiredStateEffectProvider  requires a host that can preserve desired state and definitive superseded outcomes. A reminder is an external effect, so replayed event handlers must not directly mutate it. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Transactions/ExternalEffectIntent.cs ,  AtomicEventEffectIntent.cs ,  ReminderEffectIntent.cs ,  ReminderDesiredStateEffectProvider.cs .

title: Recovery
description: Retries and pending work across providers.
text:
Recovery and retries 
 A retry must preserve the original operation identity and exact serialized event batch. The atomic store returns its prior receipt only after matching request identity, participant bytes, route fence, current ownership, and deletion fences. Changing any of those inputs is a conflict, not a new attempt at the same operation. 
 Recovery surfaces 
 
 
 
 Pending work 
 Recovery contract 
 
 
 
 
 Selected command 
 Operation recovery checks current route admission and persisted completion evidence before resuming. 
 
 
 Event-only subscriber 
 Delivery state and claim leases identify work that can be retried after a worker exits. 
 
 
 External effect 
 IExternalEffectIntentStore.ListPendingAsync  and  ExternalEffectDispatcher.RecoverPendingAsync  resume work with the original idempotency key. 
 
 
 Projection 
 Provider queue or marker state retains a handoff until the consumer applies and acknowledges it. 
 
 
 
 Provider implementations add their own journals, route pins, and retention rules. SQL Server keeps transaction evidence in its database. KurrentDB-based routes may coordinate KurrentDB and SQL state through a broker journal; this is not a distributed transaction across both systems. 
 Incident handling 
 First establish the committed receipt or current stream head. Then inspect pending delivery, effect, and projection records. Preserve operation IDs, request identities, route epochs, and provider receipts while investigating. Do not delete evidence merely to unblock a retry. See  troubleshooting  and  deployment checklist . 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Stores/IAtomicEventTransactionStore.cs ,  Transactions/IEventOnlyOrchestrationDelivery.cs ,  ExternalEffectIntent.cs ; provider recovery types in  Troolio.SqlServer/ ,  Troolio.KurrentDB/ , and  Troolio.KurrentDB.SqlServer/ .

title: Agents package
description: Agent definition and run actors.
text:
Agents package 
 Troolio.Agents  models agent definitions and runs as event-sourced actors. It provides framework contracts and actors; it does not choose a model provider, tool runtime, credential store, or execution policy for the host. 
 Definition actor 
 IAgentActor  accepts  RegisterAgent ,  UpdateAgentDefinition ,  SetAgentEnabled , and run lifecycle registration commands. Its events include  AgentRegistered ,  AgentDefinitionUpdated ,  AgentEnabledChanged ,  AgentRunStarted , and  AgentRunCompleted .  GetAgentDefinition  and  GetAgentMetrics  query the projected actor state. The definition records the agent's identity and configuration; the host decides who may modify it. 
 Run actor 
 IRunActor  accepts  RunAgentDefinition ,  StartRun ,  ResumeRun ,  CancelRun ,  RecordAgentResponse , and  RecordAgentFailure . The run event stream records start, resume, completion, failure, cancellation, and individual agent outcomes.  GetRunState  returns a  RunSnapshot ;  GetRunStatus  returns the current status. A run ID is the durable correlation key across external execution and actor updates. 
 Install with  dotnet add package Troolio.Agents --version 10.0.6 , then register the actor assembly in the Orleans host and configure a compatible store. Build an application service around these contracts for scheduling, tool permissions, model calls, and idempotent delivery. Keep credentials and sensitive prompts out of public event payloads unless your retention and erasure design permits them. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Agents/AgentContracts.cs ,  RunContracts.cs ,  AgentActor.cs ,  RunActor.cs .

title: SQL Server integration
description: SQL Server transactions, queues, routes, and recovery.
text:
SQL Server integration 
 Troolio.SqlServer  provides SQL Server implementations for atomic event transactions, selected-route evidence, projection queues, orchestration state, effect intents, and recovery. Install with  dotnet add package Troolio.SqlServer --version 10.0.6  when SQL Server is the persistence authority for a chosen route. 
 Choose the contract 
 ISqlAtomicConnectionFactory  supplies database connections.  ISqlAtomicEventCodec  controls the persisted event format.  ISqlAtomicCommitPolicy  decides whether a participant may commit; discoverable policy variants provide additional review.  SqlAtomicTransactionEngine  implements commit and recovery paths, including contextual and no-op variants. Projection consumers apply committed handoffs through  ISqlAtomicProjectionApply . 
 The package includes disposable schema helpers for tests and reference deployments. They are not a substitute for an application-owned migration, locking, indexing, backup, and retention plan. A serving host must provide connection credentials, trusted route admission, actor authorization, erasure fences, and durable operation evidence. Check the selected route's required capabilities before directing commands to it. 
 Operating a route 
 Run migrations before traffic. Review stream families, ancillary writes, transaction isolation, deadlock handling, and exact event serialization. Monitor pending projection work, receipts, and route epoch changes. Retain completion evidence at least as long as commands can be retried. See  atomic commit ,  route authority , and  recovery . 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.SqlServer/SqlAtomicContracts.cs ,  SqlAtomicTransactionEngine*.cs ,  SqlAtomicProjectionConsumer.cs ,  SqlAtomicRouteClusterLeaseAuthority.cs .

title: KurrentDB integration
description: KurrentDB append and selected-route integration.
text:
KurrentDB integration 
 Troolio.KurrentDB  provides event-stream adapters for ordinary append and selected routes, projection queue support, host pinning, committed-effect handling, and recovery checks. Install with  dotnet add package Troolio.KurrentDB --version 10.0.6  when the application uses KurrentDB streams. 
 Ordinary append 
 KurrentOrdinaryAppendAdapter  is governed by  ITrustedKurrentOrdinaryAppendAuthority  and  IKurrentOrdinaryAppendPolicy . The host supplies a trusted client, credentials, stream naming, ownership checks, and a policy for concurrent writes and deletion. Do not infer atomic multi-stream guarantees from an ordinary append. 
 Selected route 
 KurrentSelectedActorStore  uses a selected actor policy and event codec. Route admission, host pinning, recovery, and projection work have separate authority contracts. Review their implementation and configure a serving cohort before promoting a route. The combined  KurrentDB + SQL Server  package supplies a broker journal and coordination pieces when SQL-backed evidence is needed. 
 Operations 
 Protect event credentials and stream ACLs, define maximum event sizes and retention, and watch append conflicts and projection lag. Preserve exact event bytes and operation IDs through retries. A KurrentDB append and an external effect are separate durability domains; use  effect intents  and provider idempotency for side effects. 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.KurrentDB/KurrentOrdinaryAppendAdapter.cs ,  KurrentSelectedActorStore.cs ,  KurrentProjectionQueue.cs ,  KurrentRouteAdmissionAuthority.cs ,  KurrentMemoryOnlySelectedOperationRecovery.cs .

title: KurrentDB with SQL Server
description: SQL journals and broker coordination for KurrentDB.
text:
KurrentDB with SQL Server 
 Troolio.KurrentDB.SqlServer  coordinates selected KurrentDB routes with SQL Server journals, admission evidence, projection consumption, and pending effect records. Install with  dotnet add package Troolio.KurrentDB.SqlServer --version 10.0.6  alongside the matching KurrentDB and SQL Server adapters when this route is chosen. 
 Coordination model 
 A trusted write broker owns operation journal decisions and talks to the KurrentDB append authority.  SqlKurrentBrokerOperationJournal  records durable operation evidence.  TrustedKurrentAdmissionGate  uses process and cohort snapshots to decide whether a worker may serve the route.  SqlKurrentBrokerSuccessorTakeover  supports controlled successor admission after a prior broker exits.  KurrentSqlProjectionConsumer  applies projection records through an application supplied  IKurrentSqlProjectionApply . 
 KurrentDB and SQL Server do not share a distributed transaction here. A crash between systems is resolved using journals, idempotent retries, and recovery checks. The host must preserve broker identity, journal retention, SQL migrations, KurrentDB access, and a policy for uncertain outcomes. Do not erase pending evidence to force a successor to start. 
 Review before deployment 
 Verify that both provider versions are 10.0.6; configure secure credentials and trusted transport; test broker failure at each append/journal boundary; monitor pending journals and projection lag. Read  recovery  and  deployment checklist . 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.KurrentDB.SqlServer/TrustedKurrentWriteBrokerHost.cs ,  SqlKurrentBrokerOperationJournal.cs ,  TrustedKurrentAdmissionGate.cs ,  SqlKurrentBrokerSuccessorTakeover.cs ,  KurrentSqlProjectionConsumer.cs .

title: Security and retention
description: Ingress trust, credentials, erasure, and evidence lifetime.
text:
Security and retention 
 Troolio supplies contracts for actor messages and persistence, while the application host owns the security boundary. Authenticate requests before routing, authorize each command and target actor, and pass current principal evidence to selected routes. Correlation metadata is useful for tracing but is not an authorization token. 
 Data and credentials 
 Keep database, KurrentDB, broker, and external-provider credentials in a secret manager controlled by the host. Apply transport security and least privilege at every provider connection. Events may be retained for replay; design payloads so private data has an explicit minimization, encryption, retention, and erasure policy. Consider snapshots, projection copies, journals, and backups together when fulfilling deletion requirements. 
 Evidence lifetime 
 An operation receipt, route fence, effect intent, or broker journal may be required to recognize a retry. Retain that evidence for the maximum supported retry horizon, then expire it under a documented process. Erasure and deletion fences must be checked under the same authority as ordinary appends and selected commits. A retry cannot bypass a current deletion fence just because a matching historical receipt exists. 
 Review the third-party notices inside each NuGet package before redistribution. See  route authority ,  external effects , and  deployment checklist . 
 
 Source note:   Troolio.Core/Stores/IAtomicEventTransactionStore.cs ,  Troolio.Core/Transactions/TrustedAtomicCommandIngressAdapter.cs , SQL erasure and retention interfaces, package readmes and notices.

title: Testing applications
description: Test actor logic, provider guarantees, and recovery.
text:
Testing applications 
 Test a Troolio application at the contract boundaries it actually deploys. A unit test can check event decisions and replay; it cannot prove store atomicity, route admission, or crash recovery. 
 Useful test layers 
 
 Actor logic:  issue commands, inspect emitted events, replay them, and verify queries. Cover duplicate creation, stale versions, and invalid transitions. 
 Store conformance:  reject a changed batch with the same operation ID, stale expected versions, stale route epochs, and deleted owners. Prove that ancillary streams, projection handoffs, and receipt commit together. 
 Subscriber and effect recovery:  crash between claim and completion, retry a provider with the same idempotency key, and verify a definitive terminal receipt. 
 Provider integration:  use real SQL Server or KurrentDB for locking, transactions, migration, credentials, and broker failover checks. 
 Package consumer:  restore the exact public package versions into an empty-cache .NET 10 project and compile a host with the adapters it actually uses. 
 
 The repository's  Tests/ ,  Troolio.Agents.Tests/ , and  probes/ProductionPackageConsumer/  offer examples of framework acceptance. Adapt them to application-specific actor and provider policies. See  first actor ,  atomic commit , and  recovery . 
 
 Source note:  repository test projects and 10.0.6 public consumer evidence in  releases/10.0.6/publication.json .

title: Upgrade and migration
description: Move a host to 10.0.6 with replay, schema, and route checks.
text:
Upgrade and migration 
 Troolio 10.0.6 is the first public five-package cohort: Core plus Agents, SQL Server, KurrentDB, and the combined KurrentDB/SQL adapter. Existing hosts on Core 10.0.5 should review package changes and provider requirements before upgrading. The new adapter IDs do not automatically activate routes or migrate data. 
 Prepare 
 
 Inventory the current Troolio and Orleans versions, actor assemblies, stream formats, serializers, schemas, and hosted workers. Pin all chosen Troolio packages to 10.0.6. 
 Back up event streams, SQL journals, projections, and operation evidence. Record the current route epoch and deployment fingerprint if a selected path is already in use. 
 Build the application against the new packages and run actor replay tests with representative historical events. Check event type names and serialized bytes before any production rollout. 
 Apply application-owned database migrations and verify connection, lock, ownership, retention, and erasure policies. Do not use disposable test schemas as production migrations. 
 Test projection catch-up, retry identity, effect idempotency, and a worker crash near each provider boundary. 
 
 Roll out 
 Deploy compatible hosts and admit the reviewed serving cohort. For selected routes, promote the route epoch under its authoritative store and prevent older workers from writing. Watch append conflicts, projection backlog, effect intents, and broker journals. Keep rollback procedures tied to a verified state of streams and schema; event format changes may need a forward fix rather than a binary downgrade. 
 See  packages ,  deployment checklist , and  recovery . 
 
 Source note:  package metadata, selected route authority contracts, provider schema helpers, and  releases/10.0.6/package-manifest.json .

title: Troubleshooting
description: Investigate conflicts, pending work, and uncertain outcomes.
text:
Troubleshooting 
 Start with the operation ID and the authoritative provider record. A client timeout alone does not establish whether the command committed. 
 
 
 
 Symptom 
 Check 
 
 
 
 
 Version conflict 
 Current stream head, expected version, and actor ownership. 
 
 
 Stale route 
 Route key, epoch, deployment fingerprint, silo admission, and promotion record. 
 
 
 Duplicate operation rejected 
 Canonical request identity and exact serialized event batch; a changed retry is invalid. 
 
 
 Projection lag 
 Persisted handoff or queue marker, consumer checkpoint, and application apply errors. 
 
 
 Pending external effect 
 Intent, provider availability, stable idempotency key, and terminal receipt. 
 
 
 Broker takeover blocked 
 SQL journal, KurrentDB stream evidence, trusted process roster, and predecessor state. 
 
 
 
 Do not retry with a new operation ID until the original outcome is known. Do not clear projection markers, intent rows, or broker journals to make a dashboard green. Preserve logs with correlation IDs and route epochs while investigating; avoid logging payload secrets. After determining the authoritative outcome, follow the provider's recovery procedure and test the same failure in a staging environment. 
 See  recovery ,  route authority , and the specific  integration guide . 
 
 Source note:  transaction recovery interfaces and provider journal, projection, and admission implementations.

title: Deployment checklist
description: Checks for a production host and providers.
text:
Deployment checklist 
 Use this checklist when promoting a Troolio host that serves persistent actor traffic. 
 Build and compatibility 
 
 Pin all installed Troolio packages to 10.0.6 and use a compatible .NET 10 / Orleans 10 host. 
 Register the actor assemblies and the selected store/serializer explicitly. 
 Run package restore and integration tests against the same provider versions used in production. 
 
 Authority and storage 
 
 Authenticate and authorize ingress, actor targets, and selected routes. 
 Apply schema migrations and verify database transaction, locking, stream naming, and indexes. 
 Set the route epoch, reviewed deployment fingerprint, and serving silo/broker admission. 
 Define event retention, deletion fences, receipt lifetime, backups, and restoration drills. 
 
 Work after commit 
 
 Configure projection consumers, delivery workers, and retry scheduling. 
 Register external-effect providers with durable idempotency and pending-intent recovery. 
 Monitor queue lag, stale route rejects, append conflicts, operation receipts, and broker journals. 
 Test crashes before and after event append, receipt creation, projection claim, effect dispatch, and broker handoff. 
 
 An adapter package supplies code, not a production route by itself. The host owns the policies and operational controls. Start with  host setup , then  packages  and  recovery . 
 
 Source note:  package contracts and acceptance evidence in  releases/10.0.6/ .

title: Packages and compatibility
description: NuGet packages, versions, and compatibility.
text:
Packages and compatibility 
 Troolio 10.0.6 targets .NET 10 and Orleans 10. Keep all installed Troolio packages on the same version. The five packages are available on NuGet.org: 
 
 
 
 Package 
 Use 
 
 
 
 
 Troolio.Core 
 Actor, event, store, transaction, orchestration, and projection contracts. 
 
 
 Troolio.Agents 
 Agent definition and run actors. 
 
 
 Troolio.SqlServer 
 SQL Server transaction, projection, route, and effect adapters. 
 
 
 Troolio.KurrentDB 
 KurrentDB append, selected-route, queue, and recovery adapters. 
 
 
 Troolio.KurrentDB.SqlServer 
 SQL coordination for KurrentDB broker, journal, admission, and projections. 
 
 
 
 Install Core first: 
 dotnet add package Troolio.Core --version 10.0.6
 
 Add only integrations your application uses. The package references resolve their declared dependencies; the host must still register compatible services and own provider configuration. The combined KurrentDB/SQL package coordinates two stores using durable evidence; it does not create a distributed transaction. 
 Each package includes license/readme metadata. Review the bundled notices and provider requirements before redistribution or deployment. See  getting started  and  host setup . 
 
 Release evidence:  all five 10.0.6 IDs were indexed on NuGet.org; an empty-cache .NET 10 consumer restored and built with zero warnings or errors, and package DLLs matched the accepted release artifacts.

title: Glossary
description: Terms used across Troolio guides.
text:
Glossary 
 
 
 
 Term 
 Meaning 
 
 
 
 
 Actor path 
 Stable identity of one actor, used in commands, ownership checks, and transaction participants. 
 
 
 Stream 
 Ordered event history for one stream name and version sequence. 
 
 
 Event 
 Immutable fact produced by a command and later replayed to reconstruct state. 
 
 
 Projection 
 Consumer that turns committed events into a read-oriented view. 
 
 
 Handoff 
 Durable marker or queue record connecting committed events to a projection consumer. 
 
 
 Operation ID 
 Stable identifier for one command attempt and its retries. 
 
 
 Request identity 
 Canonical SHA-256 digest of the original command identity and payload. 
 
 
 Participant 
 Actor/stream, expected version, and events included in one closed atomic batch. 
 
 
 Route fence 
 Route key, epoch, and deployment fingerprint checked during selected commit. 
 
 
 Completion receipt 
 Durable evidence of what committed for an operation. 
 
 
 Event-only closure 
 Bounded planning of causal subscriber events before a selected commit. 
 
 
 External-effect intent 
 Durable record of a side effect to perform after event commit with a stable idempotency key. 
 
 
 Broker journal 
 Durable evidence coordinating a KurrentDB write broker with SQL state. 
 
 
 
 Follow  selected command route  for the full request path or  recovery  for retry semantics.

title: Release notes: 10.0.6
description: What shipped in 10.0.6 and how it was verified.
text:
Release notes: 10.0.6 
 Troolio 10.0.6 publishes five packages for .NET 10 and Orleans 10: Core, Agents, SqlServer, KurrentDB, and KurrentDB.SqlServer. The release moves the accepted framework package cohort to public NuGet.org, including the four new adapter IDs. 
 Verification 
 The five accepted archives were checked for package identity, dependency metadata, license/readme files, and exact archive and DLL hashes before upload. NuGet.org accepted all five packages and the Core symbol package. After indexing, a fresh empty-cache .NET 10 project restored all five from NuGet.org alone and built with zero warnings or errors. Downloaded package DLL hashes matched the accepted manifest. 
 Adoption 
 Pin the same 10.0.6 version for all Troolio packages. Read  packages  for installation and  deployment checklist  for host responsibilities. The selected atomic path requires explicit authority, persistence capability, and recovery policy; ordinary actor use remains a separate route. 
 The public site documents current source contracts and provider boundaries. Consult the package metadata and your application's migration plan before upgrading an existing deployment.
